subject: Penetration testing scope — delineation across Hosted, Dedicated, Private/VPC, On-prem
messages:
From: Rajiv Mehta <rajiv.mehta@streamline.io>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-04-12T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Pen test report — scope clarification request

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the quick demo last week. As part of Streamline's security review we asked for Redwood's most recent penetration test report and a short statement on what deployment models are covered by that test (Hosted API, Dedicated/reserved capacity, Private/VPC, and customer on-prem deployments). Our InfoSec team needs to understand whether the pen test findings apply to the Hosted environment only or also to Dedicated and Private offerings — specifically any differences in network boundary, customer-managed components, and where remediation responsibility lies.

Can you share the report (or attestation) and a one-paragraph scope description we can include in our SIG questionnaire? I attached our standard pen-test request PDF for reference.

Thanks,
Rajiv
Rajiv Mehta
Senior Security Engineer — Streamline
Attachment: streamline_pen_test_request.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Rajiv Mehta <rajiv.mehta@streamline.io>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-04-12T10:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pen test report — scope clarification request

Hi Rajiv — thanks for sending this over. We're happy to provide the pen test summary and a short scope blurb. I'll loop in our security team to confirm exact language for Dedicated and Private/VPC.

Quick answers up front:
- Our hosted environment (Redwood-hosted API) is included in our periodic third-party penetration tests; we can share the executive summary and remediation summary.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity) uses the same runtime but runs in isolated GPU pools; some network controls differ and customer network peering is not part of our standard test.
- Private/VPC and on-prem deployments have more customer-managed network boundaries — our standard pen test does not cover customer-controlled network appliances or on-prem host-level configs unless included in an agreed engagement.

I'll get exact wording and a timeline for the documents. Looping in Vivek (security) and Rishi (infosec lead) to confirm.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Team — forwarding Streamline's ask (attached). They need: 1) the latest pen test report or exec summary, 2) a short, customer-facing scope statement that clearly specifies which hosting models are covered and which components are customer-managed, and 3) remediation status for high/critical findings that map to customer concerns.

Can one of you:
- Confirm the latest pen test artifact we can share (PDF exec summary ok),

I'm happy to send final note to Rajiv once approved. Low urgency but they'd like to close this for procurement next week.

Thanks — Marissa

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-04-12T14:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Pen test report — scope clarification request

Marissa / team — summary below and recommended customer-facing wording. See SEC ticket SEC-421 for remediation history and timeline. I attached the redwood_10_2025_pen_test_summary.pdf to this response.

Executive summary (for sharing):
- Artifact: third-party penetration test performed Oct 2025 by Crest/Blackice; executive summary and remediation tracker available (redwood_10_2025_pen_test_summary.pdf).
- Coverage: The test assessed Redwood's hosted control plane, inference serving runtime, and associated management interfaces running in Redwood-hosted environments (our public API endpoints and the tenancy/management layer). The test did not evaluate customer-managed network appliances, customer on-prem host OS configurations, or third-party software installed in customer-managed Dedicated or on-prem environments unless explicitly in scope for a separate, customer-specific engagement.

Customer-facing scope blurb (3–4 sentences):
"Redwood's third-party penetration test (Oct 2025) evaluated the Redwood-hosted control plane and inference serving runtime as deployed in Redwood-hosted environments. Dedicated/reserved capacity instances run the same serving runtime in isolated GPU pools managed by Redwood; however, network peering, customer VPC routing, and on-prem host configurations are customer-managed and were not part of the standard pen test. For customers requiring coverage of VPC peering, dedicated networking appliances, or on-prem hosts, Redwood offers scoped, customer-funded penetration testing engagements."
Remediation note (critical/high):
- All critical findings from Oct 2025 have been remediated and validated by the vendor as of Jan 2026. High findings are either remediated or have compensating controls in place; details are tracked in SEC-421. We can provide a redacted remediation tracker on request.

Next steps:
- If Streamline needs the full report under an NDA, we'll route the vendor report through DocuSign/NDA process.
- For Dedicated or Private/VPC coverage, propose a statement-of-work and scoped pentest engagement (we can estimate within 5 business days).

Links / artifacts: SEC ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SEC-421
Attachment: redwood_10_2025_pen_test_summary.pdf

-Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Head of InfoSec, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Pen test report — scope clarification request

Hi Rajiv — thanks for the patience. Per Rishi's note below (copied into this thread), please find the customer-facing scope language and the executive summary attached. Quick highlights:

- The Oct 2025 third-party pen test covers Redwood-hosted control plane and inference runtime.
- Dedicated/reserved capacity runs the same runtime in isolated pools managed by Redwood; network peering and customer VPC routing are customer-managed and out-of-scope for the standard test.
- On-prem/private deployments are not covered unless a separate engagement is contracted.
- Critical issues from the Oct 2025 test were remediated and vendor-validated as of Jan 2026; high issues are tracked in SEC-421 and we can share a redacted remediation tracker on request.

I've attached the executive summary (redwood_10_2025_pen_test_summary.pdf). If you need the full vendor report we'll request approval through our NDA flow — let me know and I can start that. Alternatively, if you'd like Redwood to include VPC peering or on-prem host checks in scope, we can provide an SOW and estimate.

Would you like to schedule a short call with Rishi to walk through the scope and remediation notes?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
